status: verified private network recording; public snapshots remain unsupported

scope: Nine pinned HAR conversion groups, six host ownership/writer groups on Bun and Node22/24, five snapshot host regressions and five common-recording lifecycle groups.
Five live native network groups cover exact binary request/response bodies, empty/404/redirect outcomes, accepted routing decisions, immutable chunk prefixes and unfinished HTTP retirement.

Sixteen candidate cases use the actual pinned offline viewer on headless shell/full Chrome, with screenshots off/on and resources loaded before/during recording. Parent and child frames sharing resource URLs preserve separate CSSOM bodies and original frame references. The original application server is stopped before replay.

contracts: A recording owns canonical request occurrences, raw header/timing metadata, body jobs and resources across chunk gaps. Sealed metadata versions remain immutable; only already-admitted body cells may settle.
Original request identity survives route mutations and public history eviction. Reused browser request IDs invalidate old body ownership before canonical event filtering.

Actual browser reply or exact original session destruction releases optional body-command work; cancellation, page crash and context loss alone do not prove settlement. Healthy pages are not retired for optional trace diagnostics.

Network resources share immutable host storage and archive ownership with snapshots/sources/filmstrips. Native byte charges survive binary transfer and clear only after terminal transport ownership and ingestion acknowledgement.
Missing original response bodies remain unavailable; no fallback refetch can change application traffic or substitute later bytes.
retainedFailures: Early compile/lint attempts exposed missing command initialization, visibility and a canonical-base64 iteration lint; later locked workspace checks passed.

The first live collector batch exhausted byte credits because queued jobs reserved worst-case payloads before worker admission. Workers now acquire execution slots first and shrink reservations to actual bytes before releasing them.

The first host build caught an exact-optional-property assignment. A later controlled lifecycle fixture omitted the new recording-status reply; its watchdog was deliberately interrupted, the fixture was corrected, and the complete twelve-group batch then passed.
limitations: Public snapshots:true remains explicitly unsupported in this checkpoint; private viewer acceptance is not public API or packed snapshot acceptance.
Out-of-process snapshot frames, unsupported custom-element states, automatic runner trace policies and video remain incomplete.
Original resources loaded before recording remain absent, matching the pinned reference cases; this is not page archival or a refetch facility.
No new performance, native Linux, release or exhaustive parity claim.
